fields.finding: 2 mL of PRP obtained from each 10 mL tube; activated with 10% calcium gluconate before injection

evidence.quote: PRP was prepared from 20 mL of peripheral blood, which was divided into two 10 mL tubes, via a RegenLab Kit (RegenLab SA, Le Mont-sur-Lausanne, Switzerland). Each tube underwent a single centrifugation at 1,500 rpm for five minutes at room temperature. From each tube containing 10 mL of centrifuged blood, 2 mL of PRP was obtained per tube. The resulting PRP was activated with 10% calcium gluconate before being injected.

facts.notes: Source describes the preparation once; it is not scoped to a specific cycle.

summary.text: A 39-year-old woman with five months of amenorrhea presented with her partner for premature ovarian insufficiency and a three-year history of secondary infertility; the couple denied significant medical conditions and smoking. Baseline AMH was 0.03 ng/mL, FSH 90 mIU/mL and LH 15 mIU/mL with a confirmed POI diagnosis, no antral follicles on ultrasound and endometrial thickness 4.7 mm. The male partner, aged 40 years, had normal semen parameters.

She received intraovarian PRP injected under transvaginal ultrasound guidance with intravenous propofol sedation and antibiotics, tolerating it without pain or adverse effects. One month after the first treatment, ultrasound showed a 6 mm right-ovary follicle with AMH 0.03 ng/mL, FSH 32 mIU/mL and LH 15 mIU/mL, and a second PRP cycle was performed. Menstruation resumed three months after the last PRP; five months after the second cycle ultrasound showed antral follicles in both ovaries with AMH 0.1 ng/mL, FSH 25 mIU/mL and LH 32 mIU/mL.

Five months after the second PRP treatment, DuoStim ovarian stimulation with recombinant gonadotropin was started. The first cycle retrieved one oocyte, which fertilized but degenerated by day 3. A second cycle five days after the first retrieval yielded one mature oocyte that fertilized correctly and became a type 4B blastocyst, biopsied for PGT-A by next-generation sequencing and found to be euploid.

A frozen blastocyst was transferred after hormone replacement endometrial preparation with vaginal progesterone luteal support, and serum beta-hCG was 343 mIU/mL on day 13 after transfer with ultrasound confirming a singleton pregnancy. The pregnancy was uncomplicated; at 38 weeks and five days a cesarean delivery for breech presentation produced a healthy female infant weighing 3,420 g.
